correctness.rationale: For all real 0<r<s and every 0<u<v<1, Q_a(u)=log[-log(1-u^(1/a))] and Q_a prime=1/[a u B((-log u)/a)]. The elementary strict inequalities z<-log(1-z)<z/(1-z) establish B prime>0 and B double-prime<0, with B(0+)=0. Strict concavity/increase yields rho B(w)<B(rho w)<B(w) (rho=r/s), hence rho<Q_s prime/Q_r prime<1 and integration establishes the exact claim. B(w)->1 at infinity and B(w)~w log(1/w) at zero establish sharpness. Finite log moments and integrated quantiles prove the centered convex sandwich. Actual verify.py was executed and tests numerical instances, not universality.

value.rationale: Exact, optimal, nontrivial quantitative distortion parameters r/s and 1 for all shape pairs and all confidence-level intervals solve the natural problem of how the dispersion of log parallel lifetime changes with shape. The sharp strictly positive lower contraction bound does not follow from known qualitative star ordering. The two endpoint regimes have different distortion laws, the full continuum is classified, and the result yields a nontrivial lower centered convex-order sandwich; not just finite enumeration or arbitrary special values.
